title.en: The State, the Government, and You

text.en: We often use the words state and government as if they mean the same. In a city apartment, an elderly resident once collapsed because the medicine she needed could not be delivered in time, and the neighbours called for help from public services. Who takes responsibility, and how can we make the government work for the people? In this chapter we learn what a state is, how governments work and how citizens can take part.

A state has four features: a defined territory, a permanent population, a government and sovereignty. Without people there can be no state. Sovereignty means the state is supreme within its borders and independent of outside control. The government is the part of the state that acts on its behalf. A government can change after elections, but the state remains the same. The state is the larger concept: the citizens, the territory, the government and sovereignty together.
The Constitution makers used the words democratic and republic together. In a democracy the people choose their rulers. In a republic the head of state, the highest office, is elected and not hereditary. India, France and the United States are republics. Republics try to defend against the dominance of the majority, which means a situation in which the majority forgets the rights of minorities. George Washington showed his commitment to the republican form many years before he became the first US President in 1789. During the framing of the Constitution there was much debate on what kind of parliamentary democracy India should have.
The legislature makes laws for the country or state. Parliament for the whole country and the Vidhan Sabha or Legislative Assembly in each state, such as the one in Jharkhand, are legislatures. The executive implements the laws and takes policy decisions. It includes the prime minister, chief ministers, their ministers, and also the president and governors, whose roles are mostly formal or symbolic. The permanent officials who run departments are called bureaucrats or civil servants. The police are agents of the state who may legally use force to keep society safe. The judiciary, the courts, is the guardian of law. It settles disputes and acts as a referee when the government or others break the law, and it safeguards the Constitution through judicial review. If fundamental rights are violated, we can go to court.
India is a federal country with 28 states and 8 union territories. A single central government cannot meet the needs of everyone. So there are three tiers: the Union or Central government, the State governments, and local governments. Local governments, Panchayats in villages and municipalities in towns, are the third tier. If a village road needs repair, people go to the local government, not to the Centre. Mahatma Gandhi strongly advocated decentralisation and self-sufficient village governments called gram swaraj. Some lands, such as tribal lands, are protected by law and private companies and others cannot buy or lease them without the permission of the local community and due legal process.
In a democracy citizens have rights and duties and can make government accountable. Many departments have grievance redressal offices where you can file complaints, and the Right to Information Act allows citizens to ask officials for information, which brings transparency and accountability. You can write about an issue in print or electronic media, take part in public discussion, form groups or petition. In 1970 the Kerala government planned a hydroelectric project in Silent Valley that would have drowned evergreen forest and its wildlife. Citizens and scientists campaigned, and the plan was dropped and a national park set up. C. B. Muthamma, one of India's first women diplomats, challenged a rule that women had to resign when they married. Her story shows how a citizen can change an unfair rule. Bribery and corruption are problems we still hear about, so citizens should be alert, vote responsibly and support honest officials.

problem.en: A village road is damaged. Which tier of government should you approach first and why?

text.en: A village road is a local matter.

why.en: Match the problem with the tier.

text.en: The Gram Panchayat looks after local roads.
If the road is a state highway, the State government would be responsible.

why.en: Larger roads belong to higher tiers.

prompt.en: Distinguish between the state and the government.

requiredIdeas.en: State: territory, people, government and sovereignty.
Government: the organ that acts on behalf of the state.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking state and government are identical.

points.en: A state has territory, population, government and sovereignty.
India is a democratic republic with three tiers of government.
Legislature makes, executive implements, judiciary guards the law.
Citizens can make government accountable through RTI, courts, media and peaceful action.
